'''Julian Lee Strawther''' (born April 18, 2002) is a Puerto Rican-American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]] of the [[West Coast Conference]] (WCC).

==High school career==
Strawther played basketball for [[Liberty High School (Nevada)|Liberty High School]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tritsch |first1=Jon |title=Julian Strawther: 16 years old and about to turn legendary |url=https://www.8newsnow.com/news/julian-strawther-16-years-old-and-about-to-turn-legendary/ |website=[[KLAS-TV]] |access-date=November 17, 2021 |date=July 21, 2018}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 27.3 points and 8.8 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Meehan |first1=Jim |title=Longtime commits Julian Strawther, Dominick Harris officially sign with Gonzaga |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2019/nov/13/longtime-committs-julian-strawther-dominick-harris/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |access-date=November 17, 2021 |date=November 13, 2019}}</ref> In his senior season, he averaged 31.5 points, 11.1 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game, earning Southeast League co-MVP honors.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Orts |first1=Jason |title=2019-20 Nevada Preps All-Southern Nevada boys basketball team |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/nevada-preps/np-basketball/boys-basketball/2019-20-nevada-preps-all-southern-nevada-boys-basketball-team-1987448/ |website=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]] |access-date=November 17, 2021 |date=March 20, 2020}}</ref> Strawther scored 51 points against [[Apollo High School (Arizona)|Apollo High School]] at the HoopHall West Invitational, setting an event record.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Burlison |first1=Frank |title=HoopHall West record collected by Julian Strawther |url=https://www.burlisononbasketball.com/2019/12/hoophall-west-record-collected-by-julian-strawther/ |website=Burlison on Basketball |access-date=November 17, 2021 |date=December 8, 2019}}</ref> He left as his school's all-time leader in points and rebounds.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Powe |first1=Teresa |title=Zags Wednesday: Spotlight on Julian Strawther |url=https://pacificnwsports.com/zags-wednesday-spotlight-on-julian-strawther/ |website=Pacific Northwest Sports |access-date=November 17, 2021 |date=November 17, 2021}}</ref> A consensus four-star recruit, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] over offers from [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]], [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] and [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gordon |first1=Sam |title=Liberty basketball star Julian Strawther commits to Gonzaga |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/basketball/liberty-basketball-star-julian-strawther-commits-to-gonzaga-1644236/ |website=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]] |access-date=November 17, 2021 |date=April 18, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at Gonzaga, Strawther averaged 3.4 points per game, serving as the backup to [[Corey Kispert]]. His team reached the [[2021 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|national championship game]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gordon |first1=Sam |title=Liberty’s Julian Strawther relishes run with No. 1 Gonzaga |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/basketball/ncaa-tournament/libertys-julian-strawther-relishes-run-with-no-1-gonzaga-2308962/ |website=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]] |access-date=November 17, 2021 |date=March 19, 2021}}</ref> On November 15, 2021, he scored 18 points in an 84–57 win over [[Alcorn State Braves men's basketball|Alcorn State]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Strawther scores 18 as No. 1 Gonzaga tops Alcorn State 84–57 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401371256 |access-date=November 17, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 15, 2021}}</ref> As a sophomore, Strawther averaged 11.8 points and 5.4 rebounds per game. He declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] following the season before ultimately returning to Gonzaga.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Brewer |first1=Ray |title=Gonzaga star Las Vegas' Julian Strawther declares for NBA draft|url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2022/apr/18/las-vegas-julian-strawther-declares-for-nba-draft/ |access-date=February 1, 2023 |work=[[Las Vegas Sun]] |date=April 18, 2022}}</ref>

On January 28, 2023, Strawther scored a career-high 40 points in an 82–67 victory over [[Portland Pilots men's basketball|Portland]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Strawther has 40, No. 14 Gonzaga downs Portland 82-67 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401470430 |access-date=February 1, 2023 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 28, 2023}}</ref> In the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2023 NCAA tournament]] against [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], he made a {{convert|35|ft|adj=on}} basket for the lead with six seconds remaining, and Gonzaga held on for the win to advance to the quarterfinals.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Jubilation turns into heartbreak as UCLA loses to Gonzaga again in NCAA tournament|date=March 23, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-23/ucla-basketball-gonzaga-ncaa-tournament-sweet-16-recap|access-date=March 24, 2023}}</ref>

==National team career==
Although a native of [[Las Vegas]], Strawther represents Puerto Rico at the international level due to his mother's Puerto Rican ancestry.<ref name="graney">{{cite web |last1=Graney |first1=Ed |title=Activist nature part of Julian Strawther’s family history |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/sports-columns/ed-graney/activist-nature-part-of-julian-strawthers-family-history-2051029/ |website=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]] |access-date=November 17, 2021 |date=June 11, 2020}}</ref> At the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]], he averaged 22 points and 6.1 rebounds per game, helping his team finish in sixth place. He recorded 40 points, 10 rebounds and four assists in a loss to [[Russia men's national under-19 basketball team|Russia]] in the fifth-place game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Strawther's 40 points ranks tied for ninth in U19 World Cup history |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2019/news/strawther-s-40-points-ranks-tied-for-ninth-in-u19-world-cup-history |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=November 17, 2021 |date=July 7, 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
When Strawther was nine years old his mother, Lourdes, died from [[breast cancer]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Greene |first1=Brenna |title='Everything I do is for her': Gonzaga commit Julian Strawther's late mother impacts him on and off court |url=https://www.krem.com/article/sports/gonzaga-bulldogs/gonzaga-comitt-julian-strawther-on-moms-impact/293-e244471a-5d24-47f5-b482-4329dee4de62 |website=[[KREM (TV)|KREM]] |access-date=November 17, 2021 |date=March 9, 2020}}</ref> His older sister, Paris, played college basketball for [[UNLV Lady Rebels basketball|UNLV]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Grimala |first1=Mike |title=For prized UNLV recruiting target Julian Strawther, growing up is a team effort |url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2018/jan/16/for-top-local-recruit-julian-strawther-growing-up/ |website=[[Las Vegas Sun]] |access-date=November 17, 2021 |date=January 16, 2018}}</ref> Strawther's paternal grandfather, Edward, was a [[Lieutenant colonel (United States)|lieutenant colonel]] who served in [[World War II]], and formed the ''Las Vegas Sentinel'', one of two African-American newspapers in Nevada.<ref name=graney/>
